members.name: donation_v2
members.instructions: In this chat a persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate part of their task payment (up to $2) to Save the Children. After the chat, the persuadee privately chose how much to actually donate. People often say they will donate in the chat and then give $0, especially when their agreement was pressured, hesitant, vague or confused. Which description best fits the persuadee's behaviour?

criteria.firm_eager: Persuadee is genuinely enthusiastic about the charity early on and, on their own initiative, firmly and consistently commits to a specific amount from their task payment.
criteria.firm_specific: Persuadee clearly and firmly states a specific amount they will donate from their payment (e.g. 'I will donate $0.50'), with no hedging, and does not back away.
criteria.hedged_amount: Persuadee names an amount but hedges ('I could do', 'maybe', 'I think', 'possibly', a range) or just goes along with the persuader's suggestion.
criteria.reluctant_token: Persuadee first refused or said they need the money, and only after pressure agreed to a tiny token amount (a few cents).
criteria.confused: Persuadee seems confused about the task: talks about donating more than the payment (e.g. $5, $50), donating via a website or later, asks the persuader to donate, or mixes up roles.
criteria.vague_yes: Persuadee agrees in general that they will donate but never gives a clear amount.
criteria.undecided: Persuadee never clearly decides, or says they will think about it.
criteria.later_elsewhere: Persuadee declines to donate from this payment, but says they may donate later, elsewhere, or help in other ways.
criteria.refused: Persuadee clearly refuses to donate anything.

members.name: donation_v2b
members.instructions: Chat from a study: a persuader asks the persuadee to give some of their task earnings (at most $2) to the charity Save the Children. Once the chat ended, the persuadee made a private donation choice that the persuader never saw, and many who agreed during the chat actually gave nothing. Judge how the persuadee committed during the chat. Pick the best description.

criteria.firm_eager: Warm, sincere interest in the charity from early on, and they volunteer a definite amount from their earnings and stick with it.
criteria.firm_specific: Says plainly and without hedging exactly how much they will give from their earnings, and never retracts it.
criteria.hedged_amount: Mentions an amount only tentatively (maybe, possibly, I could, I guess, a range) or simply accepts whatever the persuader proposes.
criteria.reluctant_token: Initially declined or said they need the money, then under pressure agreed to only a symbolic few cents.
criteria.confused: Misunderstands the setup: promises more than the earnings (e.g. $5 or $50), plans to give via a website or at some later time, asks the persuader to give, or swaps roles.
criteria.vague_yes: Says yes to donating in general but never names a clear amount.
criteria.undecided: Never reaches a clear decision, or says they need to think it over.
criteria.later_elsewhere: Won't give from these earnings, though they might give some other time, to another cause, or help another way.
